<h1>Christos Mammides</h1>
<div class="role">Professor · Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden, Chinese Academy of Sciences</div>
<div class="tagline">I study whether conservation actually works, using satellite data, causal inference and the sounds of ecosystems to measure human impact on biodiversity.</div>

I am a conservation scientist working at the interface of spatial ecology, statistics and policy. My research evaluates the effectiveness of protected areas and other area-based conservation measures in reducing human pressures on biodiversity, often using quasi-experimental designs applied to global remote-sensing data. I also work in soundscape ecology, developing methods to monitor vocalizing animal communities from acoustic recordings in biodiverse ecosystems.

## Research themes

::: {.themes}
::: {.theme-card}
### Protected area effectiveness
Do protected areas reduce forest loss, land conversion and other human pressures? Quasi-experimental evaluations at regional to global scales.
:::

::: {.theme-card}
### Human pressure on biodiversity
Mapping and explaining human threats to lakes, wilderness, farmland and riparian zones, and testing how well remote metrics capture them.
:::

::: {.theme-card}
### Soundscape ecology
Acoustic indices and machine learning for monitoring bird communities, from Cyprus to tropical China and Australia.
:::

::: {.theme-card}
### AI in ecology and conservation
Large language models, uncertainty quantification and new computational tools for ecological research.
:::
:::

## Service

Associate Editor for *Conservation Science and Practice*, *Ecological Solutions and Evidence*, *Biodiversity and Conservation* and *Integrative Conservation*. Member of the IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas (WCPA). Expert evaluator for the EU Horizon Europe Programme and reviewer for UNEP's Global Environment Outlook (GEO-7).
